questions.prompt: How do you publish a new version of a Go module?

options.text: Tag the commit with a semantic version and push it (e.g. git tag v1.2.0)
Upload a tarball to a central registry

questions.explanation: There's no separate registry: tagging a semantic version in version control and pushing it is the publish step; consumers `go get module@vX.Y.Z`.

questions.prompt: What must change when you release v2.0.0 of a module?

options.text: The module path and imports must include the major version (/v2)
You must switch to GOPATH mode

questions.explanation: For v2+, the major version is part of the module path and import path, letting incompatible major versions coexist.

questions.prompt: How do you cross-compile a Go program for another OS and CPU?

options.text: Set the GOOS and GOARCH environment variables and run go build
Install a separate compiler per platform

questions.explanation: Pure-Go programs cross-compile by setting GOOS (target OS) and GOARCH (target CPU) — no cross-toolchain needed.

questions.prompt: Building with CGO_ENABLED=____ produces a fully static, pure-Go binary with no libc dependency.
questions.explanation: CGO_ENABLED=0 disables cgo, yielding a static binary that can run on a minimal base image like scratch.

questions.prompt: Which statements about distribution are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: go install pkg@version builds and installs a command onto your PATH
The module proxy and checksum DB make builds reproducible and verified
-ldflags -X can inject a version string at build time
You must commit compiled binaries per platform to the repo

questions.explanation: go install distributes tools, the proxy/checksum DB verify dependencies, and -ldflags -X stamps metadata. You cross-compile artifacts rather than commit them.

questions.prompt: Match each semantic version change to what it signals.

pairs.right: Copy dependencies into vendor/ for offline builds

questions.explanation: PATCH fixes, MINOR adds features, MAJOR breaks (and needs /vN), and vendoring bundles dependencies locally.
